module_title: SHM Energetics, Spring Combinations & Wave Mechanics (Intermediate)
introduction: This intermediate tier focuses on calculating energy profiles, spring force systems, progressive wave functions, and the principle of superposition creating standing waves on strings.

core_concepts.title: Combinations of Springs
core_concepts.description:
1. Series Combination: $\frac{1}{k_{\text{eq}}} = \frac{1}{k_1} + \frac{1}{k_2}$ (tension is uniform). 
2. Parallel Combination: $k_{\text{eq}} = k_1 + k_2$ (displacement is uniform).

core_concepts.title: Progressive Wave Equation
core_concepts.description: A wave traveling along the positive x-axis is described by $y = A \sin(\omega t - kx)$ or $y = A \sin(kx - \omega t)$, where the angular wave number is defined as $k = 2\pi/\lambda$.

core_concepts.title: Velocity of Transverse Waves on a String
core_concepts.description: Given by the formula $v = \sqrt{T/\mu}$, where $T$ is the tension in the string and $\mu$ is the linear mass density (mass per unit length).

core_concepts.title: Standing (Stationary) Waves
core_concepts.description: Formed by the superposition of two identical waves traveling in opposite directions. Nodes are points of permanent zero displacement, while Antinodes exhibit maximum displacement. The distance between two successive nodes is always $\lambda/2$.

important_entities.name: Beats
important_entities.significance: A phenomenon arising from the interference of two sound waves of slightly different frequencies, producing periodic variations in intensity. Crucial for tuning fork loading/filing problems.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Cutting a Spring Alters its Stiffness
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: The spring constant ($k$) is inversely proportional to the natural length of the spring ($k \propto 1/L$). If you cut a spring of constant $k$ into two equal halves, each new spring has a stiffness of $2k$, NOT $k/2$.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: To switch seamlessly between phase difference ($\Delta\phi$) and path difference ($\Delta x$) during interference calculations, always employ the direct ratio shortcut: $\Delta\phi = \frac{2\pi}{\lambda} \Delta x$.

exam_strategy_tips: For the speed of sound in gases, remember Laplace's correction: $v = \sqrt{\gamma P/\rho}$. Note that humid air is less dense than dry air, meaning the speed of sound increases on a humid day.
